question: What position is best for a patient immediately *after* a liver biopsy?

options.A: On their right side with a pillow pressing against the biopsy site
options.B: Flat on their back with legs raised high
options.C: Sitting straight up at a 90-degree angle
options.D: On their left side with knees tucked

explanation: You got it! Lying on the right side puts gentle pressure right where the needle went in, helping to prevent bleeding.

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before they get an injection of contrast dye?

options.A: Contrast dye increases the daily urine output significantly
options.B: Poor kidney function prevents the dye from reaching the joints
options.C: Kidneys must filter the dye to make bones show up white
options.D: Contrast dye can be toxic to the kidneys if clearance is slow

explanation: The kidneys have to filter out contrast dye. If a patient's kidneys aren't working well, the dye can linger and cause kidney damage, so checking lab results first is a crucial nursing duty.

question: What is a huge risk factor for depression in older adults?

options.A: Having too many visiting family members
options.B: Social isolation and loneliness
options.C: Participating in regular group exercise classes
options.D: Living in a community with active social clubs

explanation: Being cut off from people takes a heavy toll on mental and physical health. Connection is medicine!

question: Why are human reservoirs who show no symptoms harder to manage during an outbreak than sick patients?

options.A: They refuse to take any form of laboratory testing
options.B: Their immune systems are naturally immune to all treatments
options.C: The germs they carry are invisible to standard microscopes
options.D: They continue normal daily activities and spread germs unknowingly

explanation: Because healthy carriers do not feel sick, they do not isolate themselves, allowing them to pass pathogens to many people during routine interactions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: As a nurse, why would you start a patient on nasal oxygen therapy?

options.A: To treat tissue hypoxia and raise low blood oxygen levels
options.B: To deliver high-pressure aerosolized medications to the lungs
options.C: To completely replace normal breathing mechanics during sleep
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing dry mouth overnight

explanation: Spot on! We give oxygen when the body's tissues aren't getting enough of it (hypoxia), helping to bring those blood oxygen levels back up to a safe place.

question: Why does a large pleural effusion cause difficulty breathing?

options.A: The accumulated fluid compresses the lung tissue and limits expansion
options.B: The fluid forces the heart to pump blood too fast into the lungs
options.C: The excess fluid directly blocks the upper airway passages
options.D: The fluid creates an infection that stops red blood cells from carrying oxygen

explanation: Fluid taking up space in the chest cavity prevents the lung from fully expanding during inhalation, leading to shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h1)

question: What is the medical term for the very first menstrual period in a young female?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Menarche
options.C: Menopause
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Menarche is the term used to describe the onset of the first menstrual cycle during puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h1)

question: What should you do to the skin before putting on a newly diluted medicated lotion?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of oil to seal the pores
options.B: Clean and dry the skin gently
options.C: Scrub the area firmly with an antiseptic pad
options.D: Warm the skin with a heating pad for ten minutes

explanation: A gentle wash removes dirt without upsetting the skin barrier. Nice and easy!

question: What is the primary advantage of mobile health clinics in reproductive health outreach?

options.A: Providing free cars to every pregnant woman
options.B: Replacing all permanent hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Eliminating the need for community health education
options.D: Bringing family planning supplies directly to remote villages

explanation: Mobile clinics bridge the geographical gap by bringing essential services closer to people who live far from standard health facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: What treatment involves placing tiny radioactive sources directly inside or close to a cervical tumor?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Cryotherapy
options.C: Brachytherapy
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: You've got it! 'Brachy' means close—so brachytherapy places radiation right next to or inside the tumor to target bad cells while sparing healthy tissue.

question: What is the main job of the tiny bones (ossicles) inside your middle ear?

options.A: To amplify and transmit sound vibrations to the cochlea
options.B: To filter and warm incoming air before it reaches the lungs
options.C: To produce endolymph and maintain fluid pressure in the inner ear
options.D: To equalize air pressure between the ear canal and the throat

explanation: The malleus, incus, and stapes work together like a tiny lever system to boost the strength of sound waves as they travel from the air into the fluid-filled inner ear. Brilliant work!

question: Which of the following is an example of objective nutritional documentation?

options.A: Patient hates hospital food because it tastes bland and boring
options.B: Patient reports eating fresh vegetables once a week and skipping breakfast
options.C: Patient is lazy and refuses to eat the nutritious food provided by the hospital
options.D: Patient has a terrible diet and clearly does not care about health

explanation: Objective documentation relies on factual, descriptive statements without personal opinions or judgmental language. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h7)

question: What important detail must be included when documenting an intradermal injection?

options.A: Brand name of the alcohol swab
options.B: Name of the nurse's supervisor
options.C: Patient's favorite arm preference
options.D: Exact anatomical site used

explanation: Recording the exact location is necessary so the healthcare team can find the correct spot when returning to read the test results. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which part of the brain acts as our master biological clock?

options.A: The suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.B: The pituitary gland
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: Think of the suprachiasmatic nucleus as your body's personal timekeeper! Located in the hypothalamus, it takes in light signals from your eyes to keep your daily body rhythms on track.

question: What does 'monitoring' primarily involve in community health programs?

options.A: Continuous tracking of service uptake and activities
options.B: Waiting until a five-year grant period finishes
options.C: Changing the geographic location of the clinic daily
options.D: Firing staff members who fail to meet quotas

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process of tracking day-to-day activities and service delivery metrics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: What is maceration in the context of skin care?

options.A: Skin becoming completely numb to all touch
options.B: Skin turning completely black from cold temperatures
options.C: Skin growing extra thick layers like a hard shell
options.D: Skin becoming soft and broken down from too much moisture

explanation: Maceration happens when moisture stays on the skin too long, making the tissue weak and prone to damage. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h8)

question: How does visual disability generally affect a person's life?

options.A: It prevents individuals from ever communicating verbally
options.B: It interferes with everyday functioning and independent navigation
options.C: It automatically causes complete loss of hearing ability
options.D: It restricts the person to strict bed rest in a hospital

explanation: Because vision is vital for spatial awareness and movement, losing it makes everyday tasks and independent travel challenging. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is a key assessment to keep in mind for a patient taking an anticholinergic medication?

options.A: Measuring fasting blood glucose levels
options.B: Testing visual acuity every morning
options.C: Monitoring urinary output for retention
options.D: Checking deep tendon reflexes hourly

explanation: Spot on! Because these drugs relax the bladder and can make passing urine difficult, keeping an eye on their output is a must.

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: The brand name of soap used for their bath
options.B: The patient's favorite food and religious beliefs
options.C: The cost of the hospital bed and your home address
options.D: Joints exercised, how the patient tolerated it, and any unusual findings

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing notes always focus on the clinical facts: what you moved, how they reacted, and anything out of the ordinary.

question: What substance protects the blood vessels inside the umbilical cord from getting squeezed flat?

options.A: Decidual tissue
options.B: Amniotic fluid
options.C: Chorionic villi
options.D: Wharton's jelly

explanation: Wharton's jelly is a soft, cushioned substance that acts like a built-in shock absorber for the baby's lifeline. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h3)

question: A widow visits the clinic two years after her husband passed away, unable to return to work, sleep, or stop crying daily. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Complicated grief
options.B: Acute depression
options.C: Normal mourning
options.D: Anticipatory grief

explanation: When intense grief symptoms persist for a very long time and severely disrupt daily life, it is classified as complicated grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h3)

question: When is the ideal time to initiate discussions about goals of care and advance directives?

options.A: Only when family members begin arguing over medical bills
options.B: When the patient is unresponsive and unable to participate
options.C: Right after the patient is admitted to the intensive care unit
options.D: Before a medical crisis forces rapid, stressful decision-making

explanation: Early discussions prevent rushed decisions during emergencies and give patients ample time to reflect on their choices. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A sudden infection of the ovaries following childbirth
options.B: An abnormal opening between the birth canal and bladder or rectum
options.C: A temporary swelling of the external genitalia
options.D: A complete rupture of the uterine wall during early gestation

explanation: Prolonged pressure during difficult labor cuts off blood supply, creating a hole that leads to constant leaking of urine or stool. It's a heartbreaking condition we work hard to prevent and care for.

question: Why does infection inside a bone cause tissue death much faster than infections in soft tissue?

options.A: Bone is trapped inside a rigid structure where swelling cuts off its blood supply
options.B: The periosteum actively feeds the bacteria instead of protecting the bone
options.C: Bones lack white blood cells entirely to fight off invading bacteria
options.D: Microorganisms multiply twice as fast inside hard calcium deposits

explanation: Because bone cannot expand, swelling and pus create high pressure inside the rigid bone cavity, which compresses blood vessels and starves the tissue of oxygen. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is often the earliest sign that the brain isn't getting enough blood in a heart patient?

options.A: Inability to move the tongue
options.B: A sudden change in mental status or confusion
options.C: Yellow skin color
options.D: Pain in the big toe

explanation: The brain is a drama queen when it comes to oxygen—it complains immediately! Mild confusion or restlessness is usually the very first red flag that circulation is failing.

question: What is the main thing that makes a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) different in healthcare?

options.A: Generating high profits for private shareholders
options.B: Operating independently outside direct government control
options.C: Replacing all national health ministries completely
options.D: Providing only curative hospital-based surgeries

explanation: NGOs stand out because they operate separately from government structures. This freedom lets them move quickly and help out right where communities need them most!

question: What is the core issue in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Rapid genetic overproduction of phenylalanine in the bloodstream
options.B: Severe dietary deficiency of essential fatty acids and complex lipids
options.C: Inability of the liver to convert toxic ammonia into safe urea
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing cells in the pancreas

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the beta cells in the pancreas that are responsible for making insulin.

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?

options.A: 40 percent
options.B: 20 percent
options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 60 percent

explanation: Exactly! Water is our most abundant component, making up about 60 percent of a grown adult's weight.

question: Why does quitting cigarette smoking benefit a person's sexual health?

options.A: It causes immediate weight loss and lowers blood pressure
options.B: It replaces the need for hormonal balance in older adults
options.C: It preserves delicate blood vessels and nerve endings needed for arousal
options.D: It immediately cures all forms of inherited genetic disorders

explanation: Smoking damages blood vessels and impairs circulation, so stopping smoking protects the vascular pathways required for sexual response. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h6)

question: Which lab test is used to monitor a patient taking the blood thinner warfarin?

options.A: Prothrombin Time and INR
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Activated partial thromboplastin time
options.D: Full blood count with differential

explanation: PT and INR are the go-to tests to make sure a patient on warfarin is getting just the right dose—not too thick, not too thin!

question: During passive range of motion exercises, who is responsible for moving the joint?

options.A: The physical therapist using electrical stimulation
options.B: The nurse or caregiver moves the limb
options.C: The patient uses their own muscle strength
options.D: A mechanical pulley system driven by gravity

explanation: Remember, in *passive* exercises, the patient's muscles aren't doing the work—you (the nurse or helper) gently move the joints for them to keep them flexible.

question: How does activated charcoal help treat someone who swallowed a poison?

options.A: It dilates blood vessels to speed up renal excretion
options.B: It coats the lungs to block toxic gas inhalation
options.C: It binds to toxins in the gut to prevent their absorption into the bloodstream
options.D: It neutralizes stomach acid to prevent chemical ulcers

explanation: Activated charcoal acts like a microscopic sponge, holding onto the toxins in the stomach and gut so they don't enter the bloodstream.

question: What is a major ethical debate surrounding Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) like IVF?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all genetic diseases at birth
options.B: Compulsory fertility treatment for all citizens
options.C: Fair access and what to do with unused embryos
options.D: Total absence of any legal regulations worldwide

explanation: ART often raises tough questions about fairness in who can afford it and how leftover embryos should be handled ethically. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: During a sudden storm, a boat nurse needs to assess a patient. What is the most important first step for safety?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative so the patient sleeps through the storm.
options.B: Leave the patient unattended until the vessel reaches calm waters.
options.C: Transport the patient immediately to the captain's private quarters.
options.D: Secure the patient firmly against the ship's movement during the assessment.

explanation: Well done! Keeping the patient from falling or sliding as the ship rocks is always the top safety priority during rough weather.

question: What is the final step after completing a community situation analysis?

options.A: Closing down the primary health center for renovations
options.B: Translating the findings into an actionable health plan
options.C: Waiting for another NGO to come and do the work
options.D: Destroying all survey papers to protect patient privacy

explanation: The entire purpose of gathering and analyzing situation data is to guide practical healthcare planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention?

options.A: Rehabilitating a patient after major cancer surgery
options.B: Catching an existing disease during its very early stages
options.C: Providing palliative comfort during end-of-life care
options.D: Preventing a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person

explanation: Think of primary prevention as stopping trouble before it even starts—like protecting healthy people by reducing risk factors.

question: Your patient looks nervous while you get ready to test their cranial nerves. What should you do first?

options.A: Proceed quickly with the exam to get it finished
options.B: Skip the neurological assessment entirely for the day
options.C: Administer a strong sedative medication immediately
options.D: Explain each step simply before performing it

explanation: Well done! Addressing your patient's worry with a gentle explanation builds trust and makes them feel much more comfortable.

question: What safety advice should a nurse give a patient whose vision is slightly blurred from an anti-spasmodic?

options.A: Double the next dose to build up a drug tolerance
options.B: Avoid driving or operating machinery until vision clears
options.C: Stop taking all fluids immediately to reduce swelling
options.D: Rub the eyes vigorously with a warm damp cloth

explanation: Safety first! Blurry vision makes dangerous tasks like driving a real hazard until the medication wears off.

question: Your patient suddenly starts wheezing, struggling to breathe, and breaking out in hives right after an IV medication starts. What is your very first action?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately.
options.B: Slow the infusion rate to a keep-vein-open speed.
options.C: Notify the attending physician before taking action.
options.D: Document the vital signs in the patient chart.

explanation: Brilliant nursing instinct! Always stop the flow first to keep any more of the allergen from entering their system.

question: Which of these actions breaks the rule of current, truthful documentation?

options.A: Updating the care plan after assessing a new wound
options.B: Charting routine morning vital signs before taking them
options.C: Writing a note ten minutes after giving an injection
options.D: Recording a patient's reaction right after a procedure

explanation: Spot on! Charting care before you actually do it is falsification and is dangerous and illegal.

question: Which professional is best suited to work with a nurse in creating a specialized meal plan for a patient?

options.A: Registered dietitian
options.B: Social media influencer
options.C: Hospital security guard
options.D: Pharmaceutical sales rep

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Registered dietitians are the absolute experts when it comes to planning safe, personalized diets.
